content: Statistics New Zealand, also known in Māori as Tatauranga Aotearoa, is the state sector organization responsible for managing the official statistics of New Zealand. This responsibility is granted under the authority of the Statistics Act of 1975. Prior to 1994, the organization was referred to as the Department of Statistics. The current Minister of Statistics for New Zealand is the Honorable Clayton Cosgrove. In addition to its overarching leadership role, Statistics New Zealand conducts numerous statistical programs, including the national census, which is carried out every five years. Many of the statistics generated by the organization are made freely available to the public through its official website. Furthermore, the department develops statistical classifications and standards specific to New Zealand and engages in ongoing research and development to refine and advance statistical methodologies. It also provides technical assistance to developing countries in the Pacific region, with a particular emphasis on Pacific Island nations. Statistics New Zealand is tasked with leading the development and promotion of all government statistics that comprise New Zealand's Official Statistics System. This role includes coordinating the country's first integrated program of official social statistics. The chief executive officer of Statistics New Zealand holds the title of Government Statistician. The individuals who have served in this role include: John Darwin (1980–1984) Steve Kuzmicich (1984–1992) Len Cook (1992–1999) Brian Pink (1999–2007) Geoff Bascand (2007–present) In 2005, Statistics New Zealand was ranked as the 18th most desirable employer for graduates in Australasia. This recognition is largely attributed to its Graduate Leadership Development Programme (gLDP). The gLDP is designed to enhance and cultivate future leadership capabilities within Statistics New Zealand and the broader New Zealand Public Service. The program encourages graduates to develop their leadership skills through a structured, well-supported, and innovative framework. Participants in the gLDP are provided with access to social and technical support networks, monthly workshops, peer mentoring, action learning groups, and team-based corporate projects. During the first year of the program, graduates complete three rotations to gain a comprehensive understanding of the organization. As they progress, they are given increasing responsibilities and opportunities to manage projects. Statistics New Zealand, as a learning organization, is widely recognized for its commitment to staff development, and the gLDP exemplifies this dedication. The Statistics New Zealand website explicitly states that information obtained from the organization may be freely used, reproduced, or quoted unless otherwise specified. However, in all instances, Statistics New Zealand must be acknowledged as the source of the information.
